
## Overview

This document provides a detailed technical guide for integrating CyberArk Audit logs and CyberArk Endpoint Privilege Manager (EPM) logs with Microsoft Sentinel. The purpose of this document is to describe the end-to-end integration process, including the configuration steps required in both the CyberArk platform and Microsoft Azure, to enable secure and reliable log ingestion into the Sentinel workspace.

## Approach

The integration is implemented using a structured two-phase approach. In the first phase, the CyberArk environment is prepared by configuring a Web Application within CyberArk Identity, creating an OAuth service user with the appropriate permissions, and generating the required API keys, OAuth credentials, and service endpoints necessary for exporting audit data. This phase ensures that CyberArk is properly configured to securely expose audit events for external consumption.

In the second phase, the integration is completed within Microsoft Sentinel by configuring the CyberArk Audit data connector and deploying the required Azure resources, including Azure Functions and supporting storage components. The previously generated CyberArk API details and credentials are provided during this stage to enable authenticated data collection and ingestion into the Sentinel Log Analytics workspace. The document also describes the role of Azure Functions and Azure Blob Storage in the data ingestion workflow and outlines the approach for ingesting CyberArk EPM logs using the Common Event Format (CEF) over syslog.

This guide is intended for security and cloud engineering teams responsible for implementing, operating, and maintaining CyberArk integrations with Microsoft Sentinel in enterprise environments.

## Requirements

Integrating CyberArk with Microsoft Sentinel is required to centralize CyberArk Audit, Endpoint Privilege Manager (EPM), and Privileged Session Manager (PSM) logs within the Sentinel Log Analytics workspace. This integration enables centralized monitoring, correlation, and detection of privileged access–related activities at the SIEM level. Ingesting these logs supports security monitoring, threat detection, investigation, and compliance use cases across the environment.

## CyberArk Configuration

The configuration includes setting up authentication using OAuth, creating a service user, and generating the SIEM integration details required by Microsoft Sentinel.

---

**Step 1: Create SIEM Integration in CyberArk Admin Space**

1. Log in to the **CyberArk Admin Space**.
2. Navigate to **My Environment** → **Integrations** → **Export to SIEM**.
3. Click **Create SIEM Integration**.
4. Provide a meaningful name (for example: Microsoft-Sentinel-Audit).
5. Copy the Script provided in section A,

6. Scope script isp.audit.event:read
7. And other script will be required to paste in Advanced section.

8. Save the integration.

![](file:///C:/Users/ARCHIT~1/AppData/Local/Temp/msohtmlclip1/01/clip_image001.png)![](file:///C:/Users/ARCHIT~1/AppData/Local/Temp/msohtmlclip1/01/clip_image002.png)![](data:image/png;base64,)

After creation, CyberArk generates:

- **SIEM API Key**
- **SIEM Export Endpoint URL**

Record these values securely, as they are required during the Microsoft Sentinel configuration.

**Step 2: Create OAuth Web Application in CyberArk Identity**

1. Log in to the **CyberArk Identity Admin Portal**.
2. Navigate to **Apps & Widgets** → **Web Apps**.
3. Click **Add Web App** and select **OAuth2 Server Application**.
4. Provide a name for the Application ID (for example: Sentinel-Audit-Integration).

![](data:image/png;base64,)

5. Configure the application with the following settings:

- **Grant Type**: Client Credentials
- **Token Type**: JWT
- **Signing Algorithm**: RS256

![](data:image/png;base64,)

6. For Scope Section- provide the scope copied while creating the SIEM integration for Sentinel – isp.audit.event:read

![](data:image/png;base64,)

7. Go to Advance Section – and paste the 2nd script from SIEM integration page.

![](data:image/png;base64,)

This web application will be used by Microsoft Sentinel to obtain access tokens for calling the CyberArk Audit APIs.

---

**Step 3: Create OAuth Service User**

A dedicated service user is required for API-based access.

1. In the CyberArk Identity Admin Portal, navigate to **Core Services** → **Users**.
2. Create a new user (for example: sentinel-audit-svc).
3. Set the user type as a **Service User**.
4. Enable the option for **OAuth confidential client**.

![](data:image/png;base64,)

5. After the creation of user navigate to Application Settings and select the OAuth application, and specify the username of newly created user.

![](data:image/png;base64,)

6. Go back to the Webb application and navigate to Permission Section Add the user to the list and Ensure the user has access to the required audit permissions

1.      Grant, view, run and Automatically deploy

![](data:image/png;base64,)

This service account will be used exclusively for log export.

## Microsoft Sentinel Configuration

The configuration includes deploying the required Data Connector – CyberARK Audit, complete setup with configuring authentication parameters.

---

**Step 1: Install Data connector in Microsoft Sentinel**

1. Log in to the **Azure Portal**.
2. Navigate to **Microsoft Sentinel**.
3. Go to **Content Hub**.
4. Search for **CyberArk Audit** and select the connector and install.

This data connector will securely retrieve CyberArk Audit events using API-based authentication.

---

**Step 2: Configure the CyberArk Audit Connector**

1.      Go to data connector page of CyberArk Audit

2.      Click on Deploy to Azure to complete the configuration

![](data:image/png;base64,)

3.      Fill Up the information as required

![](data:image/png;base64,)  
  

4.      Instance details –

1.      Region – WestUS3

2.      LAW name

3.      LAW Location

4.      Function Name -  Cyberark-Audit-Sentinel

5.      OAuth Username – New user created

6.      OAuth Password – Password of the user copied earlier

7.      Webb App ID -  Name of the Webb Application

5.      For last 3 parameters go back to SIEM Integrations page and select the new SIEM integration Created.

![](data:image/png;base64,)

1.      Refer to the value and paste them in Sentinel Portal Configuration

·       Identity Endpoint

·       API Base URL

·       API Key

·       Leave the rest values blank.

6.      After filling all the above details Click – Review + Create.

---

**Step 3: Provide the Premissions for the Azure function for the DCR.**

1.      Go to DCR and select the new DCR created

2.      Open Access control > Role  Assignment > Monitoring Metrics Publisher

![](data:image/png;base64,)

3.      Click NEXT and select Managed Identity and select the azure function newly created for integration.

![](data:image/png;base64,)

4.      And Review and Create.

Step 4: Verification of logs ingestion

1.      Once all setup is completed go to Sentinel Page and go to Logs section

2.      Search for the CyberArk Table and run

3.      Verify if the logs has started ingesting

---

## CyberArk EPM Data connector Integration:

·       For integration of CyberArk EPM data connector, directly go to data connector page, click on deploy on Azure and perform exact same steps.

·       A new Azure function and DCR will be created,

·       Provide the required permissions and save.

·       Check the logs ingestion in the defined table.
